BURHAN:v2p129/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.claim: The Prophet supported his descriptions of Paradise with verses: unseen delights by 32:17, the promise to work by the verses of al-Layl, and the tree's long shade by 56:30.
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.anchor: منها حين ذكر ما أعد الله تعالى لأوليائه فى الجنة فقال فيها ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر

QASHANI:92:2-6/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:2-6/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:2-6/r4.claim: Giving and piety mean renouncing what distracts from God and purifying the self of attachment to what was relinquished.
QASHANI:92:2-6/r4.anchor: آثر الترك والتجريد فرفض ما يشغله عن الحق وتكره بالسهولة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.claim: Verses 5–7 describe the character and belief that qualify a person for success in the Hereafter and ease the way to it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r4.anchor: Mentioned in these verses are the character and ideology which entitles a person to the successes of the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r3.claim: The phrase about giving while God-fearing excludes boasting and worldly motives: the giver seeks God’s pleasure and fears the Day when deeds alone avail, as illustrated at 76:7–10.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r3.anchor: the purpose of this spending in the way of God should not be to boast and brag or some other worldly motive

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r2.claim: Fear of the Hereafter and belief in reward motivate virtue; without such faith, a person lacks an urge to give or gives for worldly benefit, without divine blessing, as 107:1–3 illustrates.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r2.anchor: will be rewarded in the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.claim: The virtuous fight their base desires at every step and grow stronger through that struggle, eventually reaching the servants’ company and Paradise described at 89:29–30.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r2.anchor: gradually gain the strength needed to fight

QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r6.claim: Giving can mean giving wealth, being fair to others without demanding fairness for oneself, or avoiding what displeases God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r6.anchor: ويقال : { أعطى } الإنصاف من نفسه ، { واتقى } طلب الإنصاف لنفسه

SULAMI:v2p398#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r1.claim: The generous give up both abodes while seeking God's pleasure, avoid frivolity and doubtful matters, and persist in seeking nearness.
SULAMI:v2p398#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : أعطى الدارين ، ولم يرهما شيئا في طلب رضا الله واتقى اللغو ، والشبهات وصدق بالحسنى

TUSTARI:92:5-6/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:5-6/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
TUSTARI:92:5-6/r1.claim: Abu Bakr gave his utmost from himself and wealth, avoided settling into the natural self, and affirmed the good promise as the word of monotheism.
TUSTARI:92:5-6/r1.anchor: أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أعطى من نفسه وماله مجهوده، واتقى سكونه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.claim: The surah explains which traits bring the success and failure just mentioned in the previous surah, then warns of the Fire and distinguishes those entering it from those spared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها ، ذكر هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r8.claim: One report says the passage was revealed about Abū Bakr freeing vulnerable enslaved converts and spending for the Messenger, unlike the unbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r8.anchor: روي أنها نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه، كان عتق ضعفة عبيده الذين أسلموا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r9.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā says the surah was revealed concerning Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r9.anchor: قال عبد الله بن أبي أوفى: نزلت هذه السورة في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه، وأبي سفيان بن حرب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r10.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r10.claim: Al-Suddī relates it to Abū al-Daḥdāḥ's charitable giving and purchase of a palm from a hypocrite to secure its fruit for orphans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r10.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت في أبي الدحداح الأنصاري بسبب ما كان يعلق في المسجد صدقة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r11.claim: The two objects of أعطى are omitted because the emphasis is on praising the giver, not naming what he gave or the gift itself; the scope includes obligatory, recommended, and generous giving.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r11.anchor: وحذف مفعولي أعطى، إذ المقصود الثناء على المعطي دون تعرض للمعطى والعطية.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r12.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r12.claim: Qatada says he gave God's due; Ibn Zayd says he spent his wealth in God's path.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r12.anchor: وقال قتادة: أعطى حق الله. وقال ابن زيد: أنفق ماله في سبيل الله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r13.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads taqwa as fearing God, Mujāhid as guarding against stinginess, and Qatada as avoiding what was forbidden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r13.anchor: واتقى، قال ابن عباس: اتقى الله. وقال مجاهد: واتقى البخل. وقال قتادة: واتقى ما نهي عنه.

FARRA:v3p270/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p270/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p270/r4.claim: Abū Bakr spent his own money to buy nine enslaved men from polytheists seeking God, and he is the one who gave, feared God, and affirmed the good promise.
FARRA:v3p270/r4.anchor: اشترى تسعة رجال كانوا في أيدي المشركين من ماله يريد به الله تبارك وتعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r1.claim: The elaboration explains the differences in endeavour; one proposal makes them seek either the manifest day or covering night, and others use male/female or remembrance/opposites, but Alusi finds this far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r1.anchor: وجوز أن يراد باختلافها كون البعض طالبا لليوم المتجلي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd takes giving as spending wealth in God's path; Alusi's apparent reading is the ordinary sense of giving money.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r2.anchor: ومن هنا قال ابن زيد المراد إنفاق ماله في سبيل الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r3.claim: Qatada explains giving as fulfilling God's due, apparently the financial obligations.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة المعنى أعطى حق الله تعالى وظاهره الحقوق المالية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains taqwa as fearing God; Qatada also explains it as avoiding what He forbids or His prohibitions.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r4.anchor: واتقى أي واتقى الله عز وجل كما قال ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says taqwa here means avoiding stinginess, an interpretation Alusi dismisses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد واتقى البخل وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r5.speaker: أبو قحافة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r5.claim: A report authenticated by al-Hakim says Abu Quhafa questioned Abu Bakr for freeing weak slaves instead of strong men who could protect him; Abu Bakr said he acted for God's sake, and the verses were revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r5.anchor: عن عامر بن عبد الله ابن الزبير عن أبيه قال قال أبو قحافة لأبي بكر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf; the surah's opening verses were then revealed. A similar occasion is related for Abu al-Dahdah.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال أن أبا بكر اشترى بلالا من أمية بن خلف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r7.claim: Mentioning belief after taqwa singles out the specific after the general and maintains the rhyme; another suggestion is that listening to learn monotheism is part of giving obedience and avoiding shirk part of taqwa, but Alusi rejects it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148#3/r7.anchor: ولما كان الإيمان أمرا معتنى به في نفسه أخر عن الأتقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r6.claim: In a report from Ali, the Prophet says everyone's place in Paradise and Fire has been written, but commands them to act because each person is facilitated for the deeds for which they were created, then recites these verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r6.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال كنا مع رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r7.claim: The Prophet's instruction is to do the duties of servanthood and leave hidden divine matters to God; the descriptions apply generally despite specific occasions, since the general wording governs while those named are certainly included.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r7.anchor: عليكم شأن العبودية وما خلقتم لأجله وأمرتم به وكلوا أمور الربوبية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r8.speaker: ابن زيد وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r8.claim: Some identify the giver as Abu Bakr and the miser as Umayya ibn Khalaf; Ibn Abbas reports instead identify Abu Sufyan, while a report via al-Tusti names Abu Jahl. Alusi objects that Abu Sufyan became a firm Muslim; these are instances of the general wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r8.anchor: وقيل من أعطى أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه ومن بخل أمية بن خلف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r6.claim: Giving means spending wealth in God’s cause, and taqwa means fearing one’s Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r6.anchor: {فأما من أعطى} ماله في سبيل الله، {واتقى} ربه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r5.claim: One account says the passage was revealed about Abu Bakr buying Bilal from Umayya for a cloak and ten awqiya, then freeing him; it contrasts their efforts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r5.anchor: قيل: نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق اشترى بلالا من أمية بن خلف ببردة وعشرة أواق، فأعتقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.claim: In this story, the giver is Abu al-Dahdah, the promised good is reward, and the easier path is Paradise; the miser is the Ansari, who denies reward and is eased toward Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.anchor: {وأما من بخل واستغنى} يعني الأنصاري، {وكذب بالحسنى} يعني الثواب، {فسنيسره للعسرى} يعني النار.

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r5.claim: The fortunate person gives obedience, avoids sin, and believes the true, good promise, including the declaration of God’s oneness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r5.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى } تفصيل مبين لتشتت المساعي

BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.claim: The contrast concerns giving away wealth and hoarding it: the passage says the miser's wealth will not help him and describes the giver as giving wealth to purify himself.
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.anchor: وإنه لكذلك، الإعطاء للمال والبخل به، في آيتي الليل

BINTSHATI:v2p106/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r2.claim: Giving or withholding wealth concerns what should be spent for good and God's due to its rightful recipients through alms, charity, and generosity.
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r2.anchor: فيما يجب أن ينفق فيه المال من وجوه الخير، وأداء حق الله

BINTSHATI:v2p106/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas interprets he was mindful as he avoided stinginess.

BINTSHATI:v2p106/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r4.claim: The author rejects Ibn Abbas's reading because giving already contrasts with stinginess and the later contrast opposes giving and mindfulness to stinginess and denial.
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r4.anchor: مما يبعد أن يكون اتقى بمعنى اتقى البخل

BINTSHATI:v2p106/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r5.speaker: المفسرون
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r5.claim: The two other reported objects of mindfulness are God or the reckoning and punishment; the author regards them as closely related.
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r5.anchor: والوجهان متقاربان، فمن اتقى الله عذابه في الآخرة

BINTSHATI:v2p106/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r6.claim: Taqwa originally means protection from harm; Quranic usage associates it with avoiding sin to seek God's approval and protection from His anger and punishment.
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r6.anchor: والوقاية في الأصل الحفظ مما يضر ويؤذى

BINTSHATI:v2p107/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r1.claim: In Quranic usage, the object of taqwa is often omitted with past or present verbs, but when stated it is God; the overall usage supports fearing God, His reckoning, and His punishment.
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r1.anchor: وهذا الاستقراء يؤذن بأن الاتقاء في القرآن يغلب أن يكون اتقاء الله

BINTSHATI:v2p107/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r2.claim: Taqwa is an inward act of the heart, as shown by verses that locate it in the heart and say God receives people's piety rather than sacrificial flesh and blood.
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r2.anchor: من أفعال القلوب. بمعنى أنها لا تكون إلا في القلب

BINTSHATI:v2p107/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p107/r3.claim: The Quran contrasts taqwa with wickedness and corruption.

BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.claim: The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا النسق من البيان المعجز، يتم الربط بين المقسم به في أول السورة:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r1.claim: The giver gives what God prescribed and commanded, while the God-fearing person protects himself through obedience and avoiding sins.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى } أي وقع منه إعطاء على ما حددنا له وأمرناه به { واتقى * }

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r7.claim: The majestic plural signals how unlikely either path is: good is hard because surrounded by aversions, while reason and primordial nature warn against evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r7.anchor: وأشار بنون العظمة في كل من نجد الخير ونجد الشر إلى أن ارتكاب الإنسان لكل منهما في غاية البعد

NAHHAS:v5p241/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r9.speaker: الحسين بن واقد
NAHHAS:v5p241/r9.claim: He interprets the giver as one who pays his alms and fears his Lord.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r9.anchor: قال الحسين بن واقد فأما من أعطى زكاته واتقى ربه

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.claim: He reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal for God; the verses contrast their efforts with those of Umayya and Ubayy, identify the good as the testimony of faith, and the hard path as Hell.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ وابن عساكر عن ابن مسعود

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.claim: Giving means giving from one's bounty and fearing God; the good promise is God's compensation, ease is good, and the opposite is withholding wealth, self-sufficiency, denial, and ease toward evil.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن جرير والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.claim: He said the giver pays God's due, avoids prohibitions, and believes God's promise; the miser withholds that due, feels self-sufficient, and denies the promise.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.claim: Abu Bakr freed weak women who accepted Islam; when his father urged him to free strong protectors instead, he replied that he sought God's reward, and a family member said these verses were revealed about him.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن عساكر عن عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.claim: The Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Fire is written, but commanded people to act: each is made ready for the deeds of the saved or the wretched, then recited this passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وعبد بن حميد والبخاري ومسلم وأبو داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجة وابن مردويه وابن جرير عن علي بن أبي طالب

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.claim: Suraqa asked whether deeds were predetermined; the Prophet affirmed the decree but urged action, since each person is eased toward what he was created for, then recited the passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.anchor: وأخرج أحمد ومسلم وابن حبان والطبراني وابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.speaker: بشير بن كعب الأسلمي
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.claim: Asked about deeds, he reports the Prophet answering that they follow the written decree, yet people must act because each is eased toward what he was created for; he recited these verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن قانع وابن شاهين وعبدان كلهم في الصحابة عن بشير بن كعب الأسلمي

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.claim: Abu Qahafa urged freeing strong men who could protect Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr said he sought God's face, and the report says the passage through ‘he will be satisfied’ was revealed about him.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه عن عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas links the sura's revelation to a sale: a stingy palm owner deprived a poor household of fallen dates, then a believer traded forty palms for the tree and gave it to the family; the buyer received a promised palm in Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ان رجلا كان له نخل ومنها نخلة فرعها إلى دار رجل صالح فقير ذي عيال

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the giver fears his Lord, believes in God's promised recompense, and is eased toward good by God.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : فاما من اعطى من الفضل واتقى قال : اتقى ربه وصدق بالحسنى قال : صدق بالخلق من الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r3.claim: Qatadah says giving means paying God's due and avoiding His prohibitions.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r3.anchor: عن قتادة فاما من اعطى قال : اعطى حق الله عليه واتقى محارمه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r9.claim: The Prophet says angels call at every sunset for God to replace what spenders give and ruin what misers withhold; the report says these verses were revealed about that.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r9.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما من يوم غربت فيه شمسه الا وبجنبتيها ملكان يناديان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r1.claim: The surah's titles include al-Layl, wa-al-Layl, and wa-al-Layl idhā yaghshā, the last used by al-Bukhārī and al-Tirmidhī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r1.anchor: سميت هذه السورة في معظم المصاحف وبعض كتب التفسير ( سورة الليل ) بدون واو ، وسميت في معظم كتب التفسير ( سورة والليل ) بإثبات الواو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r2.claim: Most authorities call the surah Meccan; reports of a Medinan or partly Medinan origin are tied to a reported occasion for verse 5, when Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought a date palm from a hypocrite and gave its fruit to orphans.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r2.anchor: وهي مكية في قول الجمهور ، واقتصر عليه كثير من المفسرين . وحكى ابن عطية عن المهدوي أنه قيل : إنها مدنية ، وقيل : بعضها مدني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r3.claim: It is the ninth surah in revelation order, after al-Aʿlā and before al-Fajr, and has twenty verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r3.anchor: وعدت التاسعة في عداد نزول السور ، نزلت بعد سورة الأعلى وقبل سورة الفجر . وعدد آيها عشرون .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r4.claim: Its themes praise believers and their deeds, condemn idolaters, describe each group's reward, affirm divine guidance, and explain that the Messenger reminds people: the wary benefit while the wretched turn away and prefer worldly life, earning the greater Fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r4.anchor: احتوت على بيان شرف المؤمنين وفضائل أعمالهم ومذمة المشركين ومساويهم وجزاء كل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r5.claim: The surah also inserts signs of God's power and wondrous creation into its discussion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p377/r5.anchor: وأدمج في ذلك الإشارة إلى دلائل قدرة الله تعالى وبديع صنعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r1.claim: The summary that human efforts differ builds suspense for the detailed contrast beginning with the giver and God-fearing person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r1.anchor: وفي قوله : { إن سعيكم لشتى } إجمال يفيد التشويق إلى تفصيله بقوله : { فأما من أعطى } ( الليل : 5 ) الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r7.claim: أما introduces a conditional breakdown of the summary about divergent efforts, effectively meaning whatever the case may be; it divides a group according to the contrast being emphasized.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r7.anchor: قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم { فأما } تفريع وتفصيل للإجمال في قوله : { إن سعيكم لشتى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r1.claim: The omitted object of اتقى is understood as God; giving, piety, and belief are marks of faith, so the phrase means a believer, as in the disbelievers' admission that they did not pray or feed the poor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r1.anchor: وكذلك حذف مفعول { اتقى } لأنه يعلم أن المقدر اتقى الله .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r1.claim: The relative clause describing the giver and God-fearing person signals that facilitation is caused by those deeds and rewards them by enabling persistence; calling their deeds easy praises them, as in al-Aʿlā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r1.anchor: وإذ كان الوعد بتيسير اليسرى لصاحب تلك الصلات الدالة على أعمال الإعطاء والتقوى والتصديق بالحسنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r2.claim: Giving and miserliness are named even though covered by piety and self-sufficiency to encourage Muslims to give; giving, piety, and affirmation mark believers, while their opposites mark idolaters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r2.anchor: وإنما خص الإعطاء بالذكر في قوله : { فأما من أعطى واتقى } مع شمول { اتقى } لمفاده ، وخص البخل بالذكر في قوله : { وأما من بخل واستغنى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.claim: The passage uses الجمع مع التقسيم and four antitheses: giving versus withholding, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r1.claim: One view dates the whole surah to Mecca and says the verses concern Abu Bakr freeing weak Muslim slaves and spending for the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491/r1.anchor: ويروى أن هذه الآية نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق، وذلك أنه كان يعتق ضعفة العبيد الذين أسلموا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r1.claim: The person who gives and is mindful of God is Abū Bakr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r1.anchor: قال ابن مسعود يعني أبا بكر الصديق هذا قول الجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r3.claim: Giving means giving from one's surplus wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r3.anchor: أعطى من فضل ماله قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r4.claim: Giving can mean giving God the truth from one's heart.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r4.anchor: أعطى الله الصدق من قبله قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r5.claim: Giving can mean fulfilling God's due.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r5.anchor: أعطى حق الله عليه قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r8.claim: Taqwā means avoiding God's forbidden acts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p148/r8.anchor: اتقى محارم الله التي نهى عنها قاله قتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r1.claim: The giver gives what he is commanded to give and remains mindful of God in his affairs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417/r1.anchor: أي: أعطى ما أمر بإخراجه، واتقى الله في أموره،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r4.claim: Two angels flank each sunset, asking God to replace what a spender gives and destroy what a hoarder withholds; Abu al-Darda's report says the verses were revealed about this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r4.anchor: اللهم أعط منفقا خلفا، وأعط ممسكا تلفا". وأنزل الله في ذلك القرآن:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r2.claim: A report cited by Ibn Jarir says the verses concern Abu Bakr, who freed vulnerable women and elderly converts in Mecca to seek God's reward despite his father's advice to free stronger men for protection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r2.anchor: قال ابن جرير: وذكر أن هذه الآية نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق، رضي الله عنه:

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r11.claim: The passage begins its account of three reported occasions for revelation with Abū Bakr; the next part continues those reports.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r11.anchor: أولها: أنها نزلت في أبي بكر

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r1.claim: The preceding occasion report identifies Abū Bakr; this segment continues the source's differing accounts and argues that the passage's point is general.

KASHSHAF:92:5/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:5/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:5/r1.claim: Giving means paying one's financial obligations, and fearing God means refraining from disobedience.
KASHSHAF:92:5/r1.anchor: يعني حقوق ماله { واتقى } الله فلم يعصه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r1.claim: Giving means paying wealth's obligations, fearing God means not disobeying Him, and الحسنى may mean faith, Islam, or Paradise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766#2/r1.anchor: يعني حقوق ماله { واتقى } الله فلم يعصه

SAMIN-DURR:92:5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:92:5/r1.claim: The objects of ‘a‘ta’, ‘ittaqa’, and ‘saddaqa’ are omitted, including the complement introduced by ‘‘ala’, because the deeds themselves are the focus; the objects of withholding and self-sufficiency are omitted similarly.
SAMIN-DURR:92:5/r1.anchor: حذف مفعولي " أعطى " ومفعول " اتقى " ومفعول " صدق " المجرور ب " على "؛ لأن الغرض ذكر هذه الأحداث

SAMIN-DURR:92:5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:92:5/r2.claim: ‘We will ease him toward hardship’ may be a rhetorical counterpart to easing toward ease, or ‘nuyassir’ may mean prepare, which can apply to either ease or hardship.
SAMIN-DURR:92:5/r2.anchor: إما من باب المقابلة لقوله: { فسنيسره لليسرى } ، وإما لأن نيسره بمعنى نهيئه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r15.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r15.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the giver who is mindful of God as Abu Bakr.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r15.anchor: قال ابن مسعود يعني أبا بكر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas says giving means spending one's wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r16.anchor: أحدها : من بذل ماله , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r17.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r17.claim: Qatada says being mindful means avoiding God's prohibitions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r17.anchor: اتقى محارم الله التي نهى عنها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r18.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r18.claim: Mujahid takes being mindful as avoiding miserliness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.speaker: أبو الدرداء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.claim: Qatada reports from Khulayd, from Abu al-Darda, that the Prophet said two angels call each sunrise for God to replace the spender's gift and ruin the hoarder's wealth, then recited these verses; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.anchor: يروي قتادة عن خليد عن أبي الدرداء أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( ما من يوم طلعت فيه شمسه إلا وملكان يناديان : اللهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#6/r1.claim: The giver pays the dues owed from his wealth and fears his Lord by avoiding forbidden things.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#6/r1.anchor: ﴿ فأما من أعطى ﴾ حقوق ماله ﴿ واتقى ﴾ ربه فاجتنب محارمه

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وعامة المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r1.claim: The person who gives and is mindful of God is Abu Bakr.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r1.anchor: يعني أبا بكر رضي الله عنه وقاله عامة المفسرين

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r2.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r2.claim: Abu Bakr freed elderly women who accepted Islam; when his father urged him to free strong men for protection, he said he sought what he sought.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r2.anchor: كان أبو بكر يعتق على الإسلام عجائز ونساء

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r3.claim: Aʿṭā means giving or spending, while taqwa means avoiding God's prohibitions.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: { فأما من أعطى } أي بذل. { واتقى } أي محارم الله التي نهى عنها.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r7.claim: They explain giving as giving to people in hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r7.anchor: وقال أهل التفسير: { فأما من أعطى } المعسرين.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r8.claim: He says the giving is rendering God's due.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r8.anchor: أعطى حق الله تعالى الذي عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:92:5-7/r9.claim: He describes the giver as one truthful in heart.

QUTB-ZILAL:92:5/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:5/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:5/r1.claim: The surah gathers humanity’s diverse lives into two broad ranks: those who give, fear God, and affirm the good, and those who withhold, claim independence, and deny it.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:5/r1.anchor: تضمها في حزمتين اثنتين . وفي صفين متقابلين . تحت رايتين عامتين

QUTB-ZILAL:92:5/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:5/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:5/r2.claim: The giver offers both self and wealth and guards against God’s anger and punishment.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:5/r2.anchor: من أعطى نفسه وماله . واتقى غضب الله وعذابه

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.claim: The passage explains that the differing human paths end in praiseworthy or blameworthy outcomes, reward or punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.anchor: بين معنى اختلاف الأعمال فيما قلناه من العاقبة المحمودة والمذمومة

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r1.claim: Giving may mean spending wealth in every good cause, including freeing slaves, ransoming captives and supporting Muslims, whether obligatory or voluntary, as in 8:3, 76:8 and 92:17-20.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r1.anchor: إنفاق المال في جميع وجوه الخير من عتق الرقاب وفك الأسارى

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, giving includes fulfilling both financial rights and the self's duties of obedience to God.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r2.anchor: يتناول إعطاء حقوق المال وإعطاء حقوق النفس في طاعة الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r3.claim: Taqwa means avoiding everything improper; whether it requires avoiding minor sins was discussed under 2:2.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#3/r3.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى الاحتراز عن كل

RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r1.speaker: الأصحاب
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r1.claim: The proponents infer that God makes obedience more likely for believers and sin more likely for disbelievers, so the favored side becomes necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r1.anchor: استدل الأصحاب بهذه الآية على صحة قولهم في التوفيق والخذلان

RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r2.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r2.claim: The wording may use one opposite for another: enabling good is ease toward good, while withholding such aids is ease toward hardship.

RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r3.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r3.claim: The verse may attribute an outcome to its cause, as the idols are said to have led many people astray.

RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r4.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r4.claim: The wording may be a divine judgment and report about the person's end.

RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r5.claim: Al-Razi rejects all three replies as departures from the apparent meaning, which he says is reinforced by decisive rational proof.
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r5.anchor: عن الكل أنه عدول عن الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r6.claim: A report from ʿAli says every soul's place in Paradise or Hell is known to God; when asked whether people should then rely on fate, the Prophet said to act, since each is facilitated toward what it was created for.
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r6.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام عن النبي

RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r7.claim: Al-Qaffal answers that all people were created to worship God, citing the statement that jinn and humans were created for worship.

RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p182/r8.claim: Al-Razi calls this answer weak: the Prophet's reply means each person is facilitated toward what accords with God's prior knowledge, which cannot change.

RAZI-FULL:v31p182#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p182#2/r1.claim: The future particle may promise divine gentleness and guidance with certainty, as in the command to worship so that people may become mindful.

RAZI-FULL:v31p182#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p182#2/r2.claim: The future wording may leave room for moral change: an obedient person may sin, while a sinner may repent and obey.
RAZI-FULL:v31p182#2/r2.anchor: أن يحمل ذلك على أن المطيع

RAZI-FULL:v31p182#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p182#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p182#2/r3.claim: The future may mark delay because most reward comes in the afterlife, whose time is known only to God.

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet taught each person's destination is recorded, then urged action because everyone is eased toward what they were created for; he recited these verses.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.anchor: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib related that the Prophet said, “There is no one among you except that his place is registered

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r2.speaker: al-Zamakhsharī
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that God makes the way to obedience amiable and grants success until obedience becomes easiest, like God's expanding a guided person's breast for submission.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r2.anchor: al-Zamakhsharī says that the meaning is, “We will make it amiable to him and grant him success until obedience [to God] becomes the easiest

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r3.speaker: most
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r3.claim: Most understand giving as charitable giving; it can also mean giving God His proper due.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r3.anchor: Gives is understood by most to mean giving in charity, but can also indicate giving God His proper due (Sh).

TAB-FULL:v24p461/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p461/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p461/r1.claim: The giver spends in God's cause and in the ways God commanded from the wealth He bestowed, and fears God by avoiding His prohibitions.
TAB-FULL:v24p461/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {فأما من أعطى واتقى} [الليل: 5] قال: أعطى ما عنده واتقى، قال: اتقى ربه

TAB-FULL:v24p461/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p461/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p461/r2.claim: They gloss giving as giving one's available wealth or God's due, and piety as fearing God and avoiding His prohibitions; al-Dahhak adds remembering God.
TAB-FULL:v24p461/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {فأما من أعطى} [الليل: 5] حق الله {واتقى} [الليل: 5] محارم الله التي نهى عنها

TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن أبي الدرداء
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.claim: The Prophet says angels pray each day for God to replace what a spender gives and ruin what a miser withholds; the passage was revealed in connection with this.
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.anchor: اللهم أعط منفقا خلفا، وأعط ممسكا تلفا

TAB-FULL:v24p465/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r4.claim: A report says the verses were revealed about Abu Bakr, who freed vulnerable women converts; he told his father he sought reward with God rather than strong allies.
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r4.anchor: إنما أريد، أظنه قال: ما عند الله

TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن علي
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.claim: When asked whether people should rely on their written destinies, the Prophet commands them to act: each person is made ready for his path, and he recites the two contrasting passages.

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن علي
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.claim: Several versions say each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written, yet people must act; each is facilitated toward the work for which they were created.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.anchor: لا اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن النزال بن سبرة
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.claim: A report says every soul's outcome is written; in response to an Arab's question the Prophet says God guides each person toward good or evil, with these verses cited.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.anchor: كل ميسر لما خلق له، فمن يرد الله به خيرا

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن سعد بن عبيدة وأبي عبد الرحمن السلمي
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.claim: When asked what work means if everything is decreed, the Prophet says to act because each person is facilitated for the easier or harder path.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.anchor: اعملوا فكل ميسر: سنيسره لليسرى، وسنيسره للعسرى

TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.claim: Asked whether people act for something already decided or begin something new, the Prophet answers that every worker is made ready for his work.

TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن بشير بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.claim: The Prophet says work follows what the pens and decrees have fixed, but people must still act; each is facilitated for the work for which they were created.
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.anchor: اعملوا، فكل عامل ميسر لعمله الذي خلق له

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r1.claim: Ittaqā and taqwā function as Qur'anic analogues to the biblical fear of God, a point emphasized by Scott C. Alexander.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r1.anchor: fungieren im Koran, wie Scott C. Alexander unterstrichen hat, als Analoga zum biblischen Konzept der Gottesfurcht

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Andrae
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r2.claim: Andrae notes the central place of fear of God in late antique Christian monastic piety and its importance for the early Meccan suras.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Andrae 1932, 68–76, weist auf die zentrale Rolle der Gottesfurcht in der spätantiken christlichen Mönchsfrömmigkeit hin

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r3.claim: Although ittaqā and taqwā may sometimes have religious senses in pre-Islamic poetry, the dominant pre-Qur'anic use is secular protection-seeking.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Vereinzelt könnten ittaqā und taqwā bereits in der altarabischen Dichtung in einem religiösen Sinne verwendet worden sein, doch überwiegt vorkoranisch ganz deutlich ein profaner Gebrauch

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r4.claim: The absolute use of ittaqā in 92:5 and 73:17 likely abbreviates an accusative construction meaning to fear the Day of Judgment, as explicit in 73:17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Obwohl ittaqā in 92:5 und 73:17 absolut verwendet wird, dürfte es sich dabei wohl um eine Abbreviatur für einen akkusativischen Gebrauch wie in 73:17 handeln

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r5.claim: The collective muttaqūn appears later, in groups IIIa and IIIb; at the same time kāfirūn mentions grow and believers also appear in group IIIb.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Etwas später als ittaqā und taqwā, die ab Gruppe II belegt sind, erscheint (in den Gruppen IIIa und b) die Kollektivbezeichnung al-muttaqūn

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.claim: Istaġnā is an antonym of ittaqā and appears near taqwā in 96:7; in 80:5 the positive counterpart is piety in 80:9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Das Verb wird hier offensichtlich als Antonym zu ittaqā (V. 5) gebraucht; auch in 96:7 steht istaġnā in der Nähe von taqwā

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.claim: The first antithesis pairs virtue and vice catalogues with promises of their eschatological outcomes; first-person plural marks these promises as God's speech and authorizes them alongside the oath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.anchor: Diese Ankündigungen stehen in der ersten Person Plural, sind also eindeutig als Gottesrede markiert – ein Mittel literarischer Autorisierung

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.claim: The first stanza is symmetrical, with matching behavior-to-consequence sequences and a cross-rhyme produced by vowel variation, as Neuwirth observes.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.anchor: Die symmetrische Binnengliederung des Gesätzes in eine zweimalige Durchführung des Schemas ‚diesseitiges Verhalten – jenseitige Konsequenz’ unterstreicht ein durch Vokalvariation erzielter Kreuzreimeffekt

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.claim: The two halves are linked by paired terms: giving versus stinginess, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.anchor: V. 5 und 8 sind durch die Verwendung von Antonymen aufeinander bezogen: ʾaʿtā, „geben“ vs. baḫila, „geizen“, ittaqā, „gottesfürchtig sein“ vs. istaġnā

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

THALABI:v10p216#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p216#3/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p216#3/r7.claim: The giver spends wealth in God's way, fears his Lord and avoids His prohibitions, and believes God will replace what he gave.
THALABI:v10p216#3/r7.anchor: فأما من أعطى ماله في سبيل الله واتقى ربه واجتنب محارمه وصدق بالحسنى أي بالخلف

THALABI:v10p217/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي
THALABI:v10p217/r1.claim: At each sunset two angels call out for all creatures except humans and jinn: God should repay the spender and destroy the hoarder; the passage was revealed about this contrast.
THALABI:v10p217/r1.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما من يوم غربت شمسه إلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77#4/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77#4/r1.claim: Giving means donating from one's wealth, and piety means avoiding disobedience to the Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77#4/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: تصدق من ماله، واتقى معصية ربه (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77#4/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77#4/r2.claim: He interprets the gift as giving wealth where God is due and avoiding disobedience; he identifies the person as Abu Bakr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77#4/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أعطى المال في حق الله، واتقى الله (ومعصيته (¬2)) (¬3)، يعني الصديق

WAHIDI-QT:92:5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:5/r1.claim: The giver gives his wealth, fears his Lord, and avoids His prohibitions.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r3.claim: The giver spends wealth, fears his Lord, and avoids His prohibitions.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:2-7/r3.anchor: { فأما من أعطى } ماله { واتقى } ربه واجتنب محارمه.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r1.claim: Al-Layl keeps both its oath and answer unrestricted, unlike al-Shams, which specifies its objects; giving, piety, and الحسنى are likewise left open.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r1.anchor: جواب القسم في سورة الليل (إن سعيكم لشتى) مطلق أيضا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r2.claim: Omitting both what is given and its recipient makes giving comprehensive, whether one gives wealth, obedience, or oneself; other verses name one object while leaving the other open.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r2.anchor: حذف المفعولين دليل على العموم والإطلاق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p368/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p368/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p368/r1.claim: An omitted object differs from a verb used intransitively: omission applies when syntax requires a recoverable object, while transitive verbs can be treated as intransitive when no specific object is intended.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p368/r1.anchor: تنزيل المتعدي منزلة اللازم: لا يحتاج إلى مفعول

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p368/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p368/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p368/r2.claim: Here أعطى and اتقى remain general: اتقى means to guard oneself, and without an object it especially indicates guarding against miserliness.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p368/r2.anchor: فأما من أعطى واتقى تدل على أنه اتقى البخل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r1.speaker: قسم من المفسرين
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r1.claim: Commentators variously identify الحسنى as Paradise, the good life, the good word, the good outcome in the Hereafter, or the sound creed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r1.anchor: قسم يقول إنها الجنة وقسم يقول الحياة الحسنى وآخر الكلمة الحسنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r2.claim: The author holds that الحسنى embraces all these meanings: it is an unrestricted adjective with no named noun, matching the surah's general wording.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r3.claim: Some attribute the sequence to a reported occasion involving a person who performed the deeds in that order, identifying him as either Abu Bakr or Ali; the author instead explains it as a progression from specific to broader qualities and from action toward belief.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p369/r3.anchor: نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه وأخرى قالت إنها نزلت في علي بن أبي طالب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p370/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p370/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p370/r1.claim: The order also serves society: giving builds mutual support, piety protects others and oneself from harm, and belief in ultimate good preserves people's rights.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p370/r1.anchor: قدم الله تعالى ما هو أنسب للمجتمع عامة: العطاء ثم الإتقاء ثم التصديق بالحسنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p370/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p370/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p370/r2.claim: Yusra means the easiest or most favorable course; its superlative feminine form is grammatically appropriate, and leaving its noun unstated keeps the promise broad across worldly and future affairs.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p370/r2.anchor: واليسرى يطلق على كل ما هو الأيسر سواء من أعمال الدنيا أو الآخرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p371/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p371/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p371/r1.claim: The promise of yusra spans easing others' affairs, making one's own affairs easy, and facilitating entry into Paradise as the outcome of the first two.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p371/r1.anchor: إذن هي ثلاثة محاور تندرج تحت (فسنيسره لليسرى)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p371/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p371/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p371/r2.claim: The prefixed س marks an assured future, a view attributed to al-Zamakhshari and many grammarians; the Prophet's ongoing ease needs no such marker, while others receive ease after the stated deeds.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p372/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p372/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p372/r1.claim: Each good quality maps to one kind of yusra: giving eases others, piety eases one's circumstances, and belief in the good outcome leads to Paradise.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p372/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p372/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p372/r2.claim: The opposing traits mirror the earlier ones; self-sufficiency breeds heedlessness and tyranny, while fasanuyassiruhu lil-usra describes hardship brought upon oneself and others, not praise for making things difficult.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p373/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p373/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p373/r1.claim: Al-usra, like al-yusra, has no specified noun, and the most severe hardship is Hell; the whole surah sustains this unrestricted pattern in its actions, actors, effort, and outcomes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p373/r1.anchor: فخط السورة إذن هو خط الإطلاق والعموم من أولها إلى آخرها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.claim: The givers seek the Hereafter, while misers seek worldly life; both the first and last life belong to God, so people should follow His guidance in each.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.anchor: لأن الذي يعطي ويتقي يريد الآخرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.claim: The lām emphasizing God's ownership suits the surah's repeated focus on wealth and possession; unlike this context, the wealth-free context of 53:25 omits it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.anchor: فسياق الآيات في سورة الليل جاء كله في الأموال وامتلاكها والتصرف فيها

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r1.claim: Giving means paying wealth's due and spending for good, including freeing slaves, feeding the needy in hardship, and supporting Muslims against enemies.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r1.anchor: hayır necdine çıkan akabeyi iktiham etmek üzere fekk-i rakabe ve darlık günlerinde bîçârelere it‘âm ve müslimîni düşmanlara karşı müdafaa ve takviye eylemek gibi vücûh-i hayra sarf

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r2.claim: Taqwa means fearing God, following obedience, and protecting oneself from evil and forbidden acts, as in the description of those who avoid major sins.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r2.anchor: Allah’tan korkup tâat yolunu tutarak kendini teşettütten, fenalıktan, menhiyyâttan sakınmış

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r8.claim: Belief in al-husnā precedes giving and taqwa in the order of being, but the text mentions those acts first for two rhetorical reasons.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r8.anchor: tertîb-i vücûdîde i‘tâ ve ittikāya mukaddemdir. O fazilet ve ihsan, o tasdîke terettüb eder. Böyle iken zikirde i‘tâ ve ittikānın takdim edilmesinde iki nükte vardır.

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r9.claim: The first reason is that affirmation is required in practice as well as belief and speech: giving and taqwa are primary acts, and verbal belief without them does not earn the promise of ease.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r9.anchor: fiiliyyâtta hiç eseri zâhir olmayan tasdîke burada zikrolunacak yüsrâ vaadi terettüb etmez.

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r10.claim: The believer expects the afterlife to be better, remains optimistic about good and pessimistic about evil, and accepts hardship for virtue because it ends in happiness.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r10.anchor: sonu pek güzel saadet olduğuna, rezîletin önü rahat ve lezzet

ELMALILI:92:5-11/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r11.claim: Because ihsan gives delight, such a person gives gladly, does not begrudge wealth or effort spent on good, and endures sacrifice to avoid evil.
ELMALILI:92:5-11/r11.anchor: i‘tâ ve ittikāyı huzur ve itmi’nân-ı kalb ile seve seve yapar, hayra sarfeylediği mal ve cehde acımaz

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r1.claim: The second reason for mentioning giving and taqwa first is that effects and recompense follow their causes and deeds; al-husnā is their resulting goal.
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r1.anchor: müsebbeb sebebden, ivaz mu‘avvazdan, ecr ü mükâfâta istihkak vazife ve amelden muahhar olduğu

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r14.speaker: Hâkim
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r14.claim: Al-Hakim grades as sound a report from ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father: Abu Quhafa urges Abu Bakr to free strong slaves, but Abu Bakr says he seeks his own purpose, after which the passage is revealed.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r14.anchor: Hâkim, sahih diye Âmir b. Abdullah b. Zübeyr’den, babasından rivayet etmiş

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r15.speaker: İbn Cerîr
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r15.claim: Ibn Jarir calls the transmitted report authentic and says the passage was revealed about Abu Bakr freeing the slaves; a further report specifically associates the verse about owing no one's favor with him.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r15.anchor: İbn Cerîr der ki: “Âsâr vârid olan sahîhi budur. Demişlerdir ki: Bu, Ebû Bekir âzâd ettiklerini âzâd etmesi sebebiyle onun hakkında nâzil oldu.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r1.claim: Mecca had a sharp income divide; some wealthy pagan merchants were selfish and dismissive of the poor, even asking why they should feed those God could feed (36:47), and urging one another to hoard (4:37; 57:24).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r1.anchor: bunlar, “Dilese Allah’ın doyuracağı kimseleri biz mi besleyeceğiz!” diyecek kadar küstahlaşıyor (bk. Yâsîn 36/47), birbirlerine cimriliği öğütleyecek kadar acımasız davranıyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r2.claim: Along with establishing monotheism, Meccan revelation aimed to address poverty by purging selfishness and miserliness toward the poor and vulnerable and cultivating a spirit of sharing hardships and blessings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r2.anchor: Mekke döneminde inen âyetlerin Allah’ın birliği inancının yerleştirilmesinin yanında en büyük hedefi yoksulluk sorununa el atmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r3.claim: The surah presents two character types: the generous, self-giving Muslim and, by implication, the miserly, selfish disbeliever.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r3.anchor: bunlardan ilki olan cömert ve özverili tip müslüman insanı, cimri ve bencil tip de inkârcıyı temsil etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p229/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p229/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p229/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that a palm owner repeatedly took fruit from poor children beneath a tree whose branches crossed their courtyard; the Prophet offered him a tree in Paradise, another man bought the palm for forty trees and transferred it to the Prophet, who gave it to the poor family. The surah was then revealed; Ibn Kathir calls the report very unusual.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p229/r1.anchor: فكان الرجل إذا جاء الدار فصعد إلى النخلة ليأخذ منها الثمرة فربما تقع ثمرة فيأخذها صبيان الفقير

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p229/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p229/r2.speaker: الحاكم
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p229/r2.claim: Al-Hakim reports from Abu Bakr's father that he urged Abu Bakr to free strong enslaved men who could defend him rather than weak ones; Abu Bakr said he sought God's reward, and the verses beginning “the one who gives and is mindful” were revealed about him.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p229/r2.anchor: قال أبو قحافة لأبي بكر أراك تعتق رقابا ضعافا فلو أنك أعتقت رجالا جلدا يمنعونك ويقومون دونك

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet’s instruction to act rather than rely on one’s recorded destiny, since each is facilitated toward what he was created for; he then recited these verses.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r2.anchor: عن علي قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - "ما منكم من أحد إلا كتب مقعده من الجنة ومقعده من النار"

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports that Abū Bakr’s father urged him to free strong slaves who could protect him, but Abū Bakr said he sought another purpose; the verses were revealed concerning him and his father’s advice.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r3.anchor: محمد بن إسحاق، عن محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي عتيق، عن عامر بن عبد الله، عن بعض أهله، قال أبو قحافة لابنه أبي بكر: يا بني أراك تعتق

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r3.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r3.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said every soul's destination is known to God; when companions asked whether to rely on that, he told them to act, since each person is facilitated toward what they were created for.
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r3.anchor: ويروى عن علي عليه السلام أنه قال : ( خرجنا مع رسول الله

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r2.claim: Abū al-Daḥdāḥ represents the giver who fears God, believes in the best reward, and is eased toward Paradise.
THALABI:v10p220/r2.anchor: فأما من أعطى واتقى أبو الدحداح وصدق بالحسنى يعني الثواب فسنيسره لليسرى يعني الجنة

TAB:92:5/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:5/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:5/r1.claim: The giver spends in God's cause and gives from the wealth God bestowed wherever God commanded; the God-fearing avoid His prohibitions.

TAB:92:5/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:92:5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person gives what he has and fears his Lord; another report specifies giving from God's bounty.
TAB:92:5/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   في قوله :  فأما من أعطى واتقى قال :  أعطى ما عنده

TAB:92:5/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:5/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:5/r3.claim: Qatada explains giving as fulfilling God's due and piety as avoiding what He prohibited.
TAB:92:5/r3.anchor: عن قتادة فأما من أعطى حق الله واتقى محارم الله التي نهى عنها

TAB:92:5/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:5/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:92:5/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says this describes one who remembers God and fears Him.
TAB:92:5/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  فأما من أعطى واتقى

ITQAN:v3p268/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p268/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p268/r1.claim: One ellipsis omits the object of the verb, as in 'gave and was mindful' and 'nor did He reject you.'
ITQAN:v3p268/r1.anchor: التاسع عشر حذف المفعول نحو ﴿ فأما من أعطى واتقى ﴾ ﴿ ما ودعك ربك وما قلى ﴾

NASHR:v2p81/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p81/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr opens the listed non-verse-final words on the routes that incline verse endings; for موسى he follows his usual between-vowels reading where imāla is transmitted.
NASHR:v2p81/r7.anchor: فإن أبا عمرو يفتح جميع ذلك من طريق المميلين له رءوس الآي لأنه ليس برأس آية

NASHR:v2p81/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r8.speaker: الأزرق عن ورش
NASHR:v2p81/r8.claim: Al-Azraq’s Warsh routes through Ibn Ghalbūn and others open these non-final forms; al-Taysīr and related routes read them between vowels because they are written with yāʾ, including فأما من طغى.
NASHR:v2p81/r8.anchor: والأزرق عن ورش يفتح جميعه أيضا من طريق أبي الحسن بن غلبون، وأبيه عبد المنعم ومكي

ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r1.claim: One report says the verse concerns Abū Bakr, who freed weak enslaved converts and spent his money to please the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r1.anchor: روي أنها نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه ، كان يعتق ضعفة عبيده الذين أسلموا ، وينفق في رضا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ماله

ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā says the sūra was revealed about Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb.
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله بن أبي أوفى : نزلت هذه السورة في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه ، وأبي سفيان بن حرب .

ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r3.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says it concerns Abū al-Daḥdāḥ, who gave charity in the mosque and bought a hypocrite’s palm tree for his garden to secure its fruit for orphans; the Prophet had offered him a palm in Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r3.anchor: وقال السدي : نزلت في أبي الدحداح الأنصاري بسبب ما كان يعلق في المسجد صدقة ، وبسبب النخلة التي اشتراها من المنافق بحائط له

ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r4.claim: The two objects of aʿṭā are omitted because the focus is praise of the giver, not the recipient or gift.
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r4.anchor: وحذف مفعولي أعطى ، إذ المقصود الثناء على المعطى دون تعرض للمعطى والعطية .

ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r5.claim: The wording broadly includes spending obligatory, recommended, and honorable forms of giving.
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r5.anchor: وظاهره بذل المال في واجب ومندوب ومكرمة .

ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r6.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r6.claim: Qatāda says the giver fulfills what is due to God.

ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the giver spends his wealth in God’s cause.
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : أنفق ماله في سبيل الله .

ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “and was mindful” as fearing God.
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r8.anchor: { واتقى } ، قال ابن عباس : اتقى الله .

ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r9.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r9.claim: Mujāhid glosses it as avoiding stinginess.

ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r10.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r10.claim: Qatāda glosses it as avoiding what God prohibited.
ABUHAYYAN:92:5/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة : واتقى ما نهي عنه .

ALUSI:92:5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:5/r1.claim: This section explains how endeavors differ in outcome; the alternative that they differ as pursuits of night, day, male, or female is judged remote and awkward.
ALUSI:92:5/r1.anchor: تفصيل مبين لتفرقها واختلافها في ذلك وجوز أن يراد باختلافها كون البعض طالباً

ALUSI:92:5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:5/r2.claim: The apparent meaning of giving is to give wealth.
ALUSI:92:5/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالإعطاء بذل المال

ALUSI:92:5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:5/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI:92:5/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets giving as spending one's wealth in God's cause.
ALUSI:92:5/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد المراد إنفاق ماله في سبيل الله تعالى

ALUSI:92:5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:5/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI:92:5/r4.claim: Qatāda interprets giving as paying God's due, apparently the financial dues.
ALUSI:92:5/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة المعنى أعطى حق الله تعالى وظاهره الحقوق المالية

ALUSI:92:5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:92:5/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses God-consciousness as fearing God.
ALUSI:92:5/r5.anchor: أي واتق الله عز وجل كما قال ابن عباس

ALUSI:92:5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:5/r6.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI:92:5/r6.claim: Qatāda explains it as avoiding what God forbade and His inviolable limits.
ALUSI:92:5/r6.anchor: وفي معناه قول قتادة واتقى ما نهى عنه وفي رواية محارم الله

ALUSI:92:5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:5/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI:92:5/r7.claim: Mujāhid interprets this as refraining from miserliness, a gloss al-Alūsī dismisses.
ALUSI:92:5/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد واتقي البخل وهو كما ترى

ALUSI:92:6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:6/r7.claim: Al-Alūsī prefers giving as financial worship, taqwā as all other worship through good acts and avoiding sins, and belief in al-ḥusnā as tawḥīd or comprehensive faith; together they cover all endeavors.
ALUSI:92:6/r7.anchor: ويترجح عندي أن الإعطاء إشارة إلى العبادة المالية والاتفاء إشارة إلى ما يشمل سائر

ALUSI:92:6/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r8.speaker: الحاكم
ALUSI:92:6/r8.claim: Al-Ḥākim authenticates a report: Abū Bakr's father urged him to free strong men who could defend him instead of weak slaves; Abū Bakr replied that he sought what he sought, and the passage from 92:5 to 92:19 was revealed.
ALUSI:92:6/r8.anchor: أخرج الحاكم وصححه عن عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه قال قال أبو قحافة

ALUSI:92:6/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI:92:6/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that Abū Bakr bought Bilāl from Umayya b. Khalaf for a cloak and ten awāq and freed him; verses 92:1–4 were revealed.
ALUSI:92:6/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال أن أبا بكر اشترى بلالاً من أمية بن خلف ببردة وعشرة أواق

ALUSI:92:6/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:6/r10.claim: Al-Alūsī notes the same explanation of the order applies if the revelation occasion is Abū al-Daḥdāḥ.
ALUSI:92:6/r10.anchor: وكذا على القول بأنها نزلت في أبي الدحداح

ALUSI:92:6/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:6/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:6/r12.claim: One view makes giving obedience, taqwā avoidance of sin, and al-ḥusnā the word of truth such as tawḥīd; al-Alūsī objects that giving conventionally concerns money, especially opposite withholding, and the order remains unexplained.
ALUSI:92:6/r12.anchor: وقيل المراد أعطي الطاعة واتتقي المعصية وصدق بالكلمة الدالة على الحق

ALUSI:92:10/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r5.speaker: الإرشاد
ALUSI:92:10/r5.claim: Al-Irshād says giving and withholding head the two clauses, though lower in rank than what follows, because each is foundational to the ensuing faith and piety or denial and self-sufficiency.
ALUSI:92:10/r5.anchor: لعل تصدير القسمين بالإعطاء والبخل مع أن كلا منهما أدنى رتبة مما بعد

ALUSI:92:10/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r11.claim: Despite specific reported occasions, the two descriptions apply generally because the wording is general; each person named is an included example.
ALUSI:92:10/r11.anchor: وان كان السبب خاصاً إذ العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب نعم هو قطعي الدخول

ALUSI:92:10/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r12.claim: One view identifies the giver as Abū Bakr and the miser as Umayya b. Khalaf.
ALUSI:92:10/r12.anchor: وقيل من أعطى أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه ومن بخل أمية بن خلف

ALUSI:92:10/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:92:10/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to identify them as Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb; al-Alūsī questions this because Abū Sufyān later became a strong Muslim according to Sunnis.
ALUSI:92:10/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن الأول أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه والثاني أبو سفيان بن حرب

BAGHAWI:92:5/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:5/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:5/r1.claim: The giver spends his wealth in God's cause and fears his Lord.
BAGHAWI:92:5/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى } ماله في سبيل الله ،   { واتقى } ربه

BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.claim: An anonymous report says the passage was revealed about Abu Bakr buying Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf for a garment and ten coins and freeing him; their opposed efforts are contrasted.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.anchor: قيل : نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق اشترى بلالاً من أمية ابن خلف ببردة وعشرة أوراق ،   فأعتقه

BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.claim: Ata recounts an Ansari's palm tree whose fallen dates entered a neighbor's home; the Prophet offered a tree in Paradise, the owner refused, and Abu al-Dahdah bought it with his garden and gave it to the neighbor. The report maps the giver to Abu al-Dahdah and the miser to the Ansari.
